name: RS-485 to Ethernet converter — transparent
description: A hardware converter (Waveshare, USR-TCP232, Elfin EW11, PUSR…) that passes bytes between the network and the bus without understanding them. The gateway sends RTU frames with their CRC, exactly as on a local serial port: full diagnostics, any serial protocol, listen-only possible — but usually ONE client at a time.
setup: In the converter's web page: work mode TCP Server, protocol None / Transparent (Waveshare: 'Protocol: None'; USR: 'Transparent'; Elfin EW11: 'Protocol: None').
Set the serial side to the bus's baud / parity / stop bits — the gateway cannot set them on this kind of device.
Packet interval / 'gap' at least 10 ms (or 'auto'): too short and the converter cuts a frame in two.
Only the gateway connects to it: a second client would take the line away.
